claim: One transcript-based study compared coding-agent transcripts with hypothetical baseline task times estimated using LLM-as-a-judge methods.

evidence.quote: Their workaround was to analyze coding-agent transcripts and compare them against a hypothetical baseline estimated with LLM-as-a-judge methods. The measured time savings for seven METR staff members in January 2026 ranged from roughly 2x to more than 10x, depending on the individual. Interestingly, self-reported daily estimates consistently undershot the measured gains.

section: Controlled experiments on speed and task completion
claim: A METR study reported that AI assistants slowed experienced open-source developers on large, complex projects by as much as 20%.

evidence.quote: A METR study from early 2025 found that AI assistants actually slowed experienced open-source developers working on large, complex projects by as much as 20% (METR, 2025).

claim: The study’s panel GMM models found that accumulated technical debt subsequently reduced future velocity.

evidence.quote: Panel GMM models reveal that accumulated technical debt subsequently reduces future velocity, creating a self-reinforcing cycle.

claim: One study focused on task-completion time rather than code quality.

evidence.quote: The study focused on task completion time rather than code quality.

claim: That source identified developer over-optimism, low AI reliability, and high task complexity as potential slowdown mechanisms.

evidence.quote: Becker et al. (2025) show through controlled experiments that early-2025 AI tools, including Cursor, do not help experienced open-source developers solve real day-to-day tasks faster, pointing to potential slowdown mechanisms such as developer over-optimism, low AI reliability, and high task complexity.
